GAP-42 (2026-10-16): fixed a per-round NFE budget leak in tools/eval/framework.py _solve_framework. Non-cosine schedulers treated the per-round n_cap as a partition of the budget, but n_cap is a fraction: at nfe=10/n_rounds=3, cosine [3,3,4]=10 while codimension_sheet gave [10,10,1]=21 (2.1x), linear 16, nfe_aware_memory 11. Any prior cosine-vs-math-scheduler A/B was therefore a compute comparison. Fix: _allocate_nfe_budget normalises weights + largest-remainder apportionment; cosine path byte-identical (pinned by test). Post-fix all schedulers sum to 10. IMPORTANT: codimension_sheet n_cap is [1.0,0.9997,1.0] on R1 (adapter exposes no profile_residual_fn -> ratio saturates at ~1), so its split [4,3,3] differs from cosine [3,3,4] only in the remainder position -- the A/B is near-null by construction. The real lever is wiring a residual profile g(x) into the adapter. docs/audit/gap42-scheduler-budget-conservation.md. GAP-42 follow-up (2026-10-16): equal-NFE N=20 smoke (cosine vs codimension_sheet, seed 42) -> framework FASTAs BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5 ad2205a3...), hits 3=3; baseline also identical (4 hits). ROOT CAUSE: the R1 framework does not chain rounds. _solve_framework has restart_from_endpoint=False by default and the R1 driver does not override it; even when True, _stash_endpoint_as_x0 writes dst['x0'] but LineageFlow reads prior_entry['theta'] (lineageflow.py:2400/2049). So every round blends the INITIAL theta with fresh noise and the per-round endpoint never carries forward. Measured: stock and flag-on both give digest 27036f32 for cosine/sigmoid; flag-on + theta-aware stash gives 85d2eb8e (cosine) vs aeb2a98f (sigmoid) -> scheduler becomes live. This is the likely root cause of the six dormant-lever nulls (levers changing n_cap still move output, but nothing compounds across rounds). Enabling the chain is a protocol change = user-gated; needs (1) theta-aware stash, (2) --restart-from-endpoint (default off) on the R1 driver, (3) fresh N=1000 3-seed.
